newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels report skirmishing round Kisangani.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels report skirmishing round Kisangani.

text.p: Rebels on Tuesday reported skirmishing on the approaches to Zaire's strategic third city of Kisangani but a regional military source predicted that the battle for the city may not begin immediately.

The Zairean defence ministry said the army, which is backed by mercenaries and has sown land mines round Kisangani, was on a war footing there but rejected suggestions from the rebels that they were within 10 km (six miles) of the city.
"They are around 40 km (25 miles) from Kisangani. We are still on a war footing," a ministry spokesman told Reuters.
The spokesman, however, acknowledged the fall of the port town of Moba on Lake Tanganyika and deep in copper-rich Shaba province, saying rebels seized it on Sunday.

France, meanwhile, turned the spotlight on the plight of tens of thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees somewhere to the south of Kisangani with President Jacques Chirac denouncing "a conspiracy of silence" on the unfolding humanitarian crisis.

"The humanitarian situation in Zaire is tragic. No one can ignore it any longer. No one can remain indifferent," a spokesman quoted him as telling a cabinet meeting in Paris. "We have to ask if there is not a sort of conspiracy of silence."
France has championed foreign intervention in Zaire since the start of the conflict last October.
At rebel headquarters in the eastern city of Goma, rebel spokesman Raphael Ngenda said clashes between rebel and government forces had begun around Kisangani.
Rebel radio said Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire fighters were within 10 km of Kisangani, army headquarters for the war zone.
But the regional military source told Reuters on Tuesday the closest rebel unit was still 40 km (25 miles) from Kisangani and he expected fighting for the city to start in about 48 hours.

France backs Mobutu, 66, who has presided over the declining fortunes of Zaire for 31 years. After cancer surgery last August he has spent most of his time in Europe and is now at his villa on the French Riviera.

"France appeals solemnly to the international community to take responsibility by exerting the necessary pressure to obtain a ceasefire and to implement urgently needed humanitarian intervention," Chirac was quoted as telling a cabinet meeting.

The French government strongly supports proposals by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan for an international humanitarian intervention force. The plan has received little backing. Washington on Tuesday rejected the idea for the moment.
Rebel radio said the fall of Kisangani was imminent and repeated a March 13 deadline for Zaire soldiers to give up arms.
Military analysts say should Kisangani fall, Shaba province and diamond-rich Kasai could follow in a domino effect.
The rebels, led by veteran guerrilla Laurent Kabila, have taken at least a sixth of the third largest country in Africa.
Bizima Karaha, rebel foreign affairs commissioner, said on Tuesday they had no intention of attacking Ubundu town, where 40,000 Rwandan and Burundian refugees fled over the weekend.
He said the rebels gave the international community every chance to set up a humanitarian corridor to allow refugees to head home. Ubundu is 100 km (60 miles) southeast of Kisangani.
The U.N. refugee agency said on Tuesday that about 400,000 refugees were unaccounted for in Zaire. Some of those refugees who had been found were so weak they could barely walk.
